A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable main text, equations, all 14 figures, and Appendices A–J. The additional material and shifted appendix layouts in v4 do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original neural-network score-fitting and denoising experiments on linear, circular, and curved-manifold data in Section 6 and Appendix J.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, including the nonlinear-manifold simulations in Section 6.3 and Appendix J.4.

M1.justification: The Smoothed PL-ESF definitions, score-matching objectives, denoising dynamics, and neural-network architectures remain unchanged across Sections 3–6 and Appendix J.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic coverage: uniformly and nonuniformly spaced linear data, points on a circle, and spherical-type manifolds embedded in 3 and 20 dimensions.

E2.justification: Section 6.1 retains the ESF, Smoothed PL-ESF, and NN-learned SF comparison. The ESF-versus-NN comparisons in Figures 5 and 10 also remain unchanged. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix J retain the same sample sizes, solvers, noise schedules, training budgets, and model configurations. For example, Section 6.1 still uses 20,000 initial samples and 200 Euler steps.

E4.justification: The weight-decay sweeps in Figures 2 and 10 and tangent/normal score analyses in Figures 7–9 are unchanged. No new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is reported in the PDFs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the empirical results. The statistical reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2, 4–10, and 12–14 retain matching score curves, density histograms, generated samples, and qualitative findings. No empirical result entries or reported numerical values change.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1, Eq. (64), corrects |x-x_l^2| to |x-x_l|^2 in the Gaussian-density ratio. This locally repairs a mathematical expression; the propositions, assumptions, and proof strategy are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims connecting neural-network regularization, score smoothing, interpolation, and subspace recovery, with empirical evidence on nonlinear manifolds.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.5 discusses ridge-based denoising as suggesting behavior beyond straight-line interpolation under architectural constraints. Section 7 also reframes the complex-architecture limitation around regularization effects; the other substantive limitations remain.

D1.justification: Figure 4 newly provides a link described as containing animations of denoising and score evolution. Appendix J's implementation details and the existing code URL are unchanged; the new reproducibility statement repeats existing pointers.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands its research positioning with loss-variance, capacity, and locality explanations. New A.5 compares Farghly et al., Gabriel et al., and He et al., distinguishing this work's full denoising dynamics and NN-induced smoothing from fixed-noise densities, kernel smoothing, and ridge geometry.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited grammar and terminology corrections, promotes the experiment-details footnote into the text, and adds a reproducibility statement and Appendix A.5. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All 14 figures retain their graphics. Figure 4's caption gains the animation link, and Figures 7–9 replace 'Experiment 2' with 'Section 6.1'. Appendix figures reflow, including Figure 7 moving onto a separate page and Figure 11 following its explanatory formula.

improvement.justification: v4 better explains its relationship to closely related manifold-smoothing research in Appendix A.5, corrects the squared-distance expression in Eq. (64), and improves several captions and navigation pointers. These provide a limited gain in accuracy and clarity while the central claims, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
